title: Post-hoc Top-p Expert Routing for Dynamic Compute Allocation in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models

contributions.purpose: Enable input-adaptive compute allocation in pretrained fixed-top-k MoE models without retraining.
contributions.mechanism: Post-hoc top-p expert routing, a training-free method that repurposes router softmax probabilities as a confidence signal, selecting the minimum set of experts whose cumulative probability exceeds threshold p (nucleus-style).
contributions.evaluation: Operates entirely at inference by modifying the expert selection rule on Qwen3-30B-A3B; incurs modest perplexity penalty (+0.25 vs static top-4 at matched compute).
contributions.domain: Mixture-of-Experts language models / dynamic expert routing
contributions.source_quote: First, we propose post-hoc top-p expert routing, a training-free method for dynamic expert allocation in pretrained MoE models that repurposes router probabilities as a confidence signal.

contributions.purpose: Show that top-p routing produces emergent domain-adaptive compute allocation.
contributions.mechanism: The method automatically allocates more experts to harder/reasoning tasks without task-specific tuning.
contributions.evaluation: Calibrated for average k=4 on WikiText-2, automatically increases to k=6.04 on GSM8K (+54%), achieving 87.87% accuracy vs 81.88% for static top-4, recovering 80% of the gap to full top-8.
contributions.domain: adaptive inference-time compute allocation for reasoning
contributions.source_quote: Second, we demonstrate emergent domain-adaptive compute allocation: the method automatically allocates more experts to reasoning tasks without task-specific tuning, recovering substantial performance while reducing average compute.

contributions.purpose: Characterize the router confidence signal that the method relies on.
contributions.mechanism: Analysis of router softmax entropy and layer-wise expert-count patterns.
contributions.evaluation: Router confidence is weak (86% of maximum entropy) but sufficient for coarse-grained adaptation, with consistent layer-wise patterns where early layers require more experts than late layers.
contributions.source_quote: Third, we analyze the router confidence signal, finding it is weak (86% of maximum entropy) but sufficient for coarse-grained adaptation, with consistent layer-wise patterns where early layers require more experts than late layers.

self_declared_provenance.quote: We propose post-hoc top-p expert routing: selecting the minimum set of experts whose cumulative probability exceeds a threshold p, analogous to nucleus sampling in text generation.
These methods require either training modifications or additional learned modules. In contrast, our approach applies top-p routing post-hoc to pretrained fixed-top-k models without any training.
Our work connects to this line by treating expert count as a lightweight test-time adaptation mechanism that requires no additional training or search.

notes: Reports an explicit accuracy/perplexity TRADE-OFF: the +54% expert increase and accuracy gain on GSM8K come with a +0.25 perplexity penalty vs static top-4 at matched compute; router confidence is characterized as weak (86% of max entropy).
